data.name: Vyomasana
data.gender_notes: Vyomasana is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Vyomasana is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Vyoma' meaning 'Sky' and 'Asana' meaning 'Seat'. It is believed that this name was given to the sage Vyoma who was granted a celestial seat by the gods in the heavenly realms. The name Vyomasana carries the meaning “Sage's seat” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Vyomasana usually hope their child will grow to embody sage's seat and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of enlightenment and spiritual elevation
data.etymology: Vyomasana belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sage's seat.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vyomasana total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Vyomasana holds great cultural significance in Hindu mythology as it is associated with the sage Vyoma, who is believed to have extraordinary abilities and knowledge of the cosmos. He is revered for his deep understanding of the universe, and his name has come to symbolize the vast expanse of space and the magical powers that accompany it.
data.spiritual_significance: For spiritual seekers, the name Vyomasana holds deep spiritual significance as it is often seen as a reminder of the vastness of the universe and the infinite potential within each of us. It encourages us to expand our minds and hearts, and to strive for a greater understanding of the cosmos and our place in it. The name also serves as a reminder of the ultimate reality, which is beyond the physical world and can only be reached through spiritual growth and enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Vyomasana symbolizes the infinite expansiveness of the soul, transcending the confines of earthly limitations. It embodies the desire for spiritual growth and exploration beyond the physical realm.

historical_references.reference: Vyomasana is mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic. He is the name of a celestial being and the throne on which Vishnu is said to sit during his descents on Earth.
Vyomasana is also referred to in the Puranas, a set of eighteen Hindu religious texts. It is described as the throne of Rudra (Shiva) in the cosmic dance known as Tandava.

modern_usage.modern_context: The ancient Hindu name 'Vyomasana' has gained modern relevance in the context of Ayurveda, Yoga, and Digital Health. It refers to the 'Sky Pose' or 'Celestial Pose' in Yoga, a seated asana believed to have various health benefits. The name is also associated with Ayurvedic practices, specifically the use of 'Vyomasana Oil' for therapeutic massages. In the Digital Health sector, various mobile apps and YouTube channels offer guided sessions and tutorials on practicing the Vyomasana asana for stress relief, flexibility, and overall well-being.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted individual named Aditya Vyomasana in Bali, Indonesia attributes much of their spiritual journey to their name Vyomasana, which means "Sage's seat". They believe their name has guided them on the path of righteousness.
